common_name: Pink Profusion Salvia (Reblooming Dark-Pink Meadow Sage)

planting.note: Set out potted divisions after the last frost into well-drained soil; this Walters Gardens Profusion-series selection forms a tight, rounded clump rather than running or flopping open.

directions: Shear spent spikes back by about a third as soon as the first flush fades to trigger a fast rebloom cycle through summer. Keep soil on the lean, fast-draining side, since rich or soggy ground causes floppy growth and fewer flowering stems. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in early spring to maintain the dense, uniform habit this cultivar is bred for.

common_name: White Profusion Salvia (Reblooming Pure-White Meadow Sage)

planting.note: Install after last frost in lean, well-drained soil; the companion white selection in the Profusion series bred by Walters Gardens to match the pink and violet forms for mixed drifts.

directions: Deadhead faded flower spikes promptly to push out the next round of white bloom through the growing season. Avoid high-nitrogen fertilizer, which softens stems and reduces the tidy, self-supporting habit. Lift and divide every few seasons once the center of the clump thins out, replanting the vigorous outer sections.

common_name: Violet Profusion Salvia (Reblooming Violet-Blue Meadow Sage)

planting.note: Set potted plants out after frost danger passes; violet-blue flowers sit on rosy-purple calyxes, giving a two-tone spike effect typical of this Profusion-series release.

directions: Trim the first flush of spikes down to fresh foliage once color fades to keep a near-continuous bloom cycle into fall. Plant in gritty, fast-draining soil, since this cultivar resents winter wet more than summer drought. Combine with the Pink or White Profusion selections for a matched-habit color block, as all were bred to the same compact proportions.
sources: The Garden Gateway, "New Profusion Salvia Series"

common_name: Perfect Profusion Salvia (Reblooming Icy-Blue Meadow Sage)

planting.note: Plant after the last frost in lean soil; the soft icy-blue flowers complete the four-color Profusion series alongside Pink, Violet, and White Profusion from the same Walters Gardens breeding program.

directions: Cut back the initial bloom spikes once they brown to encourage repeat flowering rather than seed set. Keep plants in full sun with sharp drainage, since crown rot is the main risk in wet winters. Refresh overgrown clumps by division in early spring, which also multiplies stock quickly since this patented selection cannot be grown true from seed.

common_name: Snow Kiss Salvia (Color Spires White-and-Pink Bicolor Meadow Sage)

planting.note: Set out after last frost; part of Proven Winners' Color Spires nemorosa-pratensis hybrid line, notable for large white flowers with a soft pink lip rather than the solid colors typical of the series.

directions: Give at least six hours of direct sun for the densest, most upright flower spikes and best bicolor contrast. Shear back after the first bloom wave to renew foliage and extend flowering into late summer. Soil should be well-drained; this hybrid tolerates drought well but blooms more heavily with occasional deep watering during extended dry spells.
sources: Proven Winners plant profile, Color Spires Snow Kiss

common_name: Hypnotic Blue Salvia (Cleveland Sage x Dorr's Sage Hybrid for Desert Gardens)

planting.note: A Mountain States Wholesale Nursery introduction (US Plant Patent 34,395) crossing Salvia clevelandii with S. dorrii; plant in spring into sharply draining, low-fertility soil typical of the Southwest.

directions: Choose a spot with reflected heat and gravelly or decomposed-granite soil, since this hybrid struggles in heavy clay or regularly irrigated beds. Withhold summer water once established, giving only occasional deep soaks during the hottest stretches to maintain the gray-green foliage and upright violet-blue spikes. Skip fertilizer entirely, as excess richness causes lank growth and fewer flowers on this low-mounding selection.
sources: Mountain States Wholesale Nursery plant profile (mswn.com, Salvia MSWNBoynton2 Hypnotic Blue, PP 34,395)

common_name: Blue Blazes Hummingbird Mint (Large Lavender-Purple Hybrid Agastache)

planting.note: A High Country Gardens hybrid between Agastache 'Desert Sunrise' and A. foeniculum; set out after frost in lean, fast-draining soil and allow two seasons to reach its large mature size.

directions: Site this hybrid where its tall, non-stop bloom spikes can stand without crowding, since it eventually forms a large, shrub-like clump. Water sparingly once roots are established, as excess moisture in winter is far more damaging than summer drought. Expect modest top growth and bloom the first year, with full height and flower density arriving in the second season.
sources: High Country Gardens plant profile, Agastache 'Blue Blazes'
Greenhouse Grower, "Agastache 'Blue Blazes' From High Country Gardens"

common_name: Just Peachy Hummingbird Mint (Soft Pink-and-Peach Agastache aurantiaca)

planting.note: Discovered at High Country Gardens in Santa Fe; plant after last frost in gritty, well-drained soil where its fine mint-scented foliage and soft peach-pink spikes have good air circulation.

directions: Keep this selection on the dry side once established, since the fine gray-green foliage is prone to rot in soggy or heavy soils. Deadhead spent spikes to extend the summer-to-early-fall bloom window and keep plants attracting hummingbirds. In colder parts of its range, leave the dried winter stems in place until spring to help protect the crown.
